text.p: Morocco said on Thursday it freed 66 prisoners from the Algeria-backed Polisario Front after appeals from Washington and Bonn.
"Responding to demands of friendly countries the United States and Germany, Morocco released 66 (Saharan) prisoners for humanitarian reasons," the Moroccan foreign ministry said in a statement.
The prisoners were flown to Tindouf, Polisario's main military base in southwest Algeria on Thursday, it said.

The Front, seeking independence of the Western Sahara from Morocco, said earlier that the Moroccan decision was in response to its release of 185 Moroccan prisoners last year following mediation by the U.S. and Argentina.

"The release of this group of prisoners is an act of humanitarian reciprocity which must not be understood as the end of the conflict," Polisario said in a statement carried by the official Algerian news agency APS.
Polisario Front guerrillas and Moroccan troops fought for control of Western Sahara for more than 17 years until a 1991 U.N. sponsored truce.
A referendum to decide the future of the former Spanish colony was originally scheduled for 1992 but has been stalled by endless arguments over who is eligible to vote.
